claims.text: The AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock is cobalt-free.
A machine-learning model can predict and control an optimized cooling schedule for additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi.
Modulated laser scan strategies or controlled cooling rates can be used to implement the optimized cooling schedule.
The ML-optimized cooling schedule will reduce thermal gradients during solidification.
Reduced thermal gradients will lower compositional segregation in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Reduced thermal gradients will lower residual stresses in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
The optimized schedule will produce a refined and more uniform microstructure.
The optimized schedule will reduce columnar grain growth.
A more uniform microstructure with less segregation and columnar grain growth will lead to fewer defects.
A more uniform microstructure with less segregation and columnar grain growth will lead to lower residual stresses.
An ML model trained on processing-structure-mechanics datasets can identify a cooling schedule that mitigates rapid thermal gradients.
Controlled cooling will minimize phase separation.
Controlled cooling will reduce defect formation associated with additive-manufacturing thermal cycling.
The ML-optimized schedule will increase strength relative to conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi.
The ML-optimized schedule will increase ductility relative to conventionally processed AlCrFeNiSi.
Conventional additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi typically produces greater segregation, residual stress, and defect density than the proposed process.
The hypothesis is limited to cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi processed in LPBF-like systems under high-cooling-rate conditions.
Powder characteristics and processing environment may alter the outcome.
The treatment can be tested by comparing otherwise identical LPBF groups using conventional and ML-optimized cooling schedules.
Failure to significantly reduce segregation and residual stress, or failure to improve mechanical properties, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention permits modulated laser scan strategies, but the conditions and experiment require scan strategy and all parameters other than cooling schedule to remain identical. Modulating scan strategy would itself change a controlled processing parameter.

The predicted outcome refers broadly to conventionally processed samples, while the baseline specifically defines conventional additive manufacturing. This leaves the comparator ambiguous between cast or other conventional fabrication and standard LPBF.
